components.css: .ds-key { position:relative; display:flex; flex-direction:column; justify-content:space-between; gap:0.7rem; aspect-ratio:1/1; width:150px; padding:0.85rem; background:#fbfaf6; border:1px solid #b9b6ab; border-radius:12px; color:#1a1c1e; box-shadow:0 4px 9px rgba(26,28,30,0.12); font-family:'Instrument Sans',system-ui,sans-serif; text-align:left; cursor:pointer; transition:border-color 160ms ease; } .ds-key:hover { border-color:var(--key-hue); } .ds-key:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #0d9488; outline-offset:3px; } .ds-key:active { transform:translateY(3px); box-shadow:0 1px 3px rgba(26,28,30,0.16); background:#f2f0e9; } .ds-key-top { display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; } .ds-key-led { width:8px; height:8px; border-radius:50%; background:var(--key-hue); box-shadow:0 0 6px 1px rgba(26,28,30,0.15); } .ds-key-num { font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',ui-monospace,monospace; font-size:0.5625rem; font-weight:500; letter-spacing:0.14em; color:#5b5d55; } .ds-key-glyph { display:block; } .ds-key-glyph svg { display:block; width:30px; height:auto; } .ds-key-name { display:block; font-weight:700; font-size:1rem; letter-spacing:-0.01em; line-height:1.15; } .ds-key-team { display:block; font-family:'IBM Plex Mono',ui-monospace,monospace; font-size:0.5625rem; font-weight:500; letter-spacing:0.13em; text-transform:uppercase; color:#5b5d55; margin-top:0.25rem; }

components.name: Semester Rail
components.description: The semester as a clean sequencer rail docked under the display module as its time axis: month ticks, past steps dim, upcoming hollow in mode color, live step solid and pulsing, patched to the screen by the Patch Lead — a 2px run rising from the live step, sweeping through smooth rounded elbows across the 96px channel, terminating in a single input jack on the module's edge. Each event mode has its own socket position and color (Code & Tell left/blue, hackathon center/teal, Demo Day right/green); only the jack in use is rendered, with a solid mode-color core. No unused jacks, no labels, no bus hardware.

narrative.overview: HackJudge is rendered as a precision pocket instrument in the Teenage Engineering lineage: a light, milled warm-gray chassis carrying a dark display module, a keyboard of square project keys, and a sequencer rail for time. It is an Operate surface first — a console a judge works in for hours — but every control is machined, labeled, and a little playful, because the instrument makers proved that pro tools can be joyful without becoming toys. The system's whole discipline is one sentence: knobs are inputs, meters are outputs. Anything the user can change earns an interactive control with real travel; anything the user merely reads earns an honest readout — on the event card, not in a stat band. Color is load-bearing, never decorative: hardware hues mark parameters, event modes are color-coded, and house teal is reserved for HackJudge itself. HackJudge is not an event-marketing surface: the events it judges (DS+X, CivicHacks, and the Code & Tell / Demo Day formats) have their own sites; this homepage is the console for the event in front of you.
keyCharacteristics: A single floating chassis (max 1120px, 22px radius) on a darker workbench ground; below 1160px it becomes the full-bleed face
Engraved micro-labels (IBM Plex Mono, uppercase, wide tracking, highlight under-shadow) instead of helper text
The dark display module is where color and motion live: one authored canvas animation per surface, mode-voiced
Square project keys with LED accents, 3px press travel, and honest dashed open-slot keys
Time rendered as a sequencer: the semester rail docks under the display module, its live step patched to the screen by a dogleg lead; step-sequencer upcoming list, engraved ledger for the past

rules.name: The Tinted-Ink Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is always tinted from the surface it sits on (warm ink on chassis, phosphor-dim on screen). Neutral gray helper text is banned.

rules.name: The Mode-Color Rule
rules.body: Event modes are color-coded: hackathon = teal, Code & Tell = blue, Demo Day = green. The active mode color lights the top-rail pictogram, the screen's mode chip, and the rail's live step and patch lead. House teal never performs a non-house job while another mode is active.

rules.name: The Engraving Rule
rules.body: Anything the device would print on its case is set in engraved mono; anything the device would show is set in the UI sans. The two never swap.

rules.name: The Travel Rule
rules.body: Pressable things move when pressed (keys 3px, transport 2px, soft keys 1px). If it can't move, it isn't a key — it's a readout.

rules.name: The Knobs-Are-Inputs Rule
rules.body: Knobs, dials, and rotary encoders are only rendered for parameters the user can change. Facts you read get honest readouts, on the event card itself.

rules.name: The No Stat-Band Rule
rules.body: Never ship a strip of big-number metric tiles that repeat what the event card already says — hero-metric bands are marketing furniture, and event marketing lives on the events' own sites (dsplusx.com, civichacks.com), not on the console.

dos: Do tint every secondary text from its surface hue (Ink Soft on chassis, Screen Dim on glass).
Do give every pressable control real travel and a state change; keep the SELECT readout live.
Do color-code modes end to end: pictogram, screen chip, playhead, sequencer LEDs.
Do reserve house teal for HackJudge itself: focus, selection, wordmark, live hackathon state.
Do render empty and idle states as instrument idles (unlit steps, dashed slots, engraved status lines).
Do keep exactly one authored motion per surface — the display module's canvas; everything else is 160ms state feedback and the live LED pulse, all reduced-motion safe.
donts: Don't ship a strip of big-number metric tiles that repeat what the event card already says — hero-metric stat bands are marketing furniture (The No Stat-Band Rule).
Don't render knobs, dials, or rotary encoders for read-only values — knobs are inputs (The Knobs-Are-Inputs Rule).
Don't use neutral gray text, gradient text, or kicker/eyebrow labels above headings.
Don't scatter motion across sections or add glow as decoration; phosphor bloom belongs to lit LEDs only.
Don't let a stock component survive inside the instrument — nav, chips, inputs, and lists are rebuilt in the machine's vocabulary.
